articles.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
articles.excerpt: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit. Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day.The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times."To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person. Meanwhile, in the central city of Dnipro, six people were injured after a communications facility was struck, he said.Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.Since Merz became chancellor in May 2025, Germany has become the single largest donor to Ukraine.

articles.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
articles.excerpt: Major bridges in Ukraine have been the target of Russian strikes over the past four days, as Moscow ramps up attacks in Ukraine's capital city.The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week.The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday.BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near one of the bridges that was targeted and explains what we know so far.More on this story: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit

articles.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
articles.excerpt: Al-Alimi was unlikely to have made the fierce announcement without the green light from Saudi Arabia, which remains the key backer of his government.Saudi Arabia has been under constant attack as the Houthis try to target the country's economic lifeblood - oil.On Sunday, Yemen's Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had launched a ballistic missile and drone attack on Aramco sites in the capital, Riyadh, and the oil-rich Khurais area in the kingdom's east."Both operations successfully achieved their objectives," the spokesman said in a statement. "The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites."It is not the first time the group has said it has hit Saudi oil sites. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment on Sunday's claimed attack, but has previously dismissed some claims as misleading, mocking the Houthis for "chasing imaginary victories".But it has once again shown the price Saudi Arabia - and, as a consequence, the global economy - could pay if it launched a new all-out war against the Houthis.In retaliation, Saudi Arabia has also been striking Houthi targets, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV channel. It said at least two people had been wounded in strikes on Sunday.On Saturday, Yemen's government also said its forces had hit Houthi targets across the country, including in Sanaa, Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the south-west.

articles.title: Brazil election goes to run-off as right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round
articles.excerpt: Image source, ReutersImage caption, Flávio Bolsonaro casts his vote at a polling station in Rio de JaneiroByIone WellsAmericas correspondent and Tinshui YeungUpdated 15 minutes agoThe right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro has won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating the incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva. But he did not obtain more than 50% of the votes required to win outright.There will be a run-off vote between these two candidates on 25 October.Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of the former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup attempt after losing the last election.The election was close, with President Lula polling slightly ahead during the campaign.
articles.summary: 图片来源：路透社。图片说明：弗拉维奥·博索纳罗在里约热内卢一处投票站投票。作者：Ione Wells（美洲通讯员）与Tinshui Yeung。更新于15分钟前。右翼候选人弗拉维奥·博索纳罗赢得了巴西总统选举第一轮投票，击败了现任左翼总统卢拉·达席尔瓦。但他未能获得直接胜选所需的超过50%的选票。两位候选人将于10月25日进行第二轮决选投票。弗拉维奥·博索纳罗是前右翼总统雅伊尔·博索纳罗之子，后者因在输掉上次选举后策划未遂政变而被判处27年监禁。此次选举竞争激烈，竞选期间卢拉总统的民调一度略微领先。

articles.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
articles.excerpt: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, A pro-government soldier standing guard on a street in Ethiopia's Tigray region on SundayByTeklemariam Bekiteditor, BBC Tigrinya, and Jack BurgessRebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said its decision to relocate was made because of concerns about risks to civilians.Two residents in Mekelle told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF forces have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services appear to have resumed in parts of the city.Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and federal government forces alongside allied fighters in parts of Ethiopia's northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.The development marks a major shift in the conflict and raises concerns among observers that the fighting could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt on Sunday with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.Tigray residents have been trying to recover from a devastating two-year civil war that ended in 2022 when the African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides.

articles.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
articles.excerpt: US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. She survived two execution attempts on Wednesday, and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.Ferrell said: "She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill, we really don't know the prognosis yet, and may not know for several days."He didn't believe she had regained consciousness at any point, adding that he has been receiving updates through her medical power of attorney rather than consulting directly with doctors.He has not been in to see her. "She is guarded. I'm not sure who may have seen her," he said.Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. But Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said he would resign on Saturday."If she recovers - she may not fully recover - and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don't know any of this," Ferrell said. "We have had no discussions about this. The Tennessee attorney general's office so far has not given us any indications of what their intentions will be."He called on the governor to commute her death sentence to a life sentence "at the very least". "She has endured a torturous attempt at executing her," he said.

articles.title: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
articles.excerpt: Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry. Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai cities for a third day on Sunday demanding that Gyanesh Kumar step down over large-scale changes to voter rolls.The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.Videos online show people being physically dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.The accusations by the women journalists include inappropriate touching by some police.Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and the home ministry must "answer for this"."Police dragged me by my hair," Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University told Reuters news agency during the protests.She said the police were resorting to "brutality".The Press Club of India has demanded immediate action on the complaints against police officers, saying it was "shocked and dismayed" by the treatment of journalists."Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy.

articles.title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
articles.excerpt: A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma."We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family.Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture."Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur".The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday. Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline."The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said.

articles.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
articles.excerpt: Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

articles.title: What to know about Brazil's election as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off
articles.excerpt: Image source, AFPImage caption, The two candidates leading in the polls are Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio BolsonaroByVanessa BuschschlüterLatin America online editorBrazilians just finished voting in a general election in which the two front-runners for the presidency bear very familiar names. Polls closed at 17:00 Brasília Time (20:00 GMT) on Sunday, with the nation's vast electronic voter system expected to deliver a result within a few hours. The incumbent, veteran left-wing leader Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva, is challenged by 11 candidates, the most prominent of whom is right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro.In the last election four years ago, Lula narrowly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro's father Jair, but the tumultuous aftermath of the election, which saw Jair Bolsonaro convicted of plotting a coup after thousands of his supporters stormed the Brazilian Congress, has had a lasting impact on the nation's political life and this election.Here's what you need to know. The man not on the ballotImage source, Nelson ALMEIDA / AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, At the launch of his campaign, Flávio Bolsonaro screened a video in which an AI-generated image of his father endorsed his candidacyJair Bolsonaro, the right-wing former army captain who governed Brazil from 2019 to 2023, has not run for president in this election. Not only is the 71-year-old barred from standing for office, he is also serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election to Lula.Due to recurrent health problems, he is currently under house arrest rather than in a cell, but he has had restrictions imposed on him prohibiting him from posting on social media or making public statements.Despite these restrictions, his shadow - and sometimes his moving and talking image - looms large over this election.

articles.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
articles.excerpt: One of the biggest demonstration happened in the capital, Madrid, where estimates of the number of participants varied widely. The city's Tenants' Union said there were 500,000, while officials put the figure at 70,000.Demonstrators held banners reading "There won't be peace for rentism" and "I study to have a future, not to have a tiny apartment". They shook the keys they were holding and chanted: "We have the keys of all the city".Some had also camped in one of the city's main squares, Puerta del Sol, for days.One protester, David, told RTVE ahead of the protest: "We're not here for pleasure or comfort. We're here out of conviction."Another protester, 26-year-old librarian Marcos Sainz, told AFP news agency that he used to share a two-bedroom flat with friends, paying 900 euros (£766) a month in rent.

articles.title: Rescuers suspend search for survivors after plane went missing off US coast
articles.excerpt: US authorities have suspended the search for six people aboard a medical transport aircraft that went missing on Saturday while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston.The Coast Guard said on Sunday evening it was ending the search off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, after 66 hours of looking for the passengers. "We express our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones," the Coast Guard said on Sunday.The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT). Authorities have notified the next of kin of those on the flight, four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals.Authorities had said earlier that they had located a "debris field" confirmed to be from the aircraft on Saturday evening.The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News. The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).Radio transmissions shows trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net. "You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?," the air traffic controller asked.
articles.summary: 美国当局已暂停搜寻一架医疗运输飞机上的六名人员，该飞机于周六在从百慕大飞往波士顿途中失踪。海岸警卫队周日晚表示，在搜寻乘客66小时后，将结束在马萨诸塞州岛屿楠塔基特附近海域的搜索。海岸警卫队周日表示：「我们向家属和亲人表达最深切的哀悼。」美国联邦航空管理局告诉BBC，他们在当地时间凌晨1点刚过（格林尼治标准时间5点）与这架湾流G-100飞机失去联系。当局已通知机上人员的近亲，机上人员包括四名加拿大公民和两名百慕大公民。当局早些时候表示，他们在周六晚间发现了一片「残骸区」，已确认来自该飞机。根据FlightAware的航班数据，这架飞机于当地时间23点40分从百慕大的L.F.韦德国际机场起飞，原定于美国东部时间凌晨1点30分（格林尼治标准时间5点30分）降落在波士顿洛根国际机场。根据海岸警卫队公布的尾号，这架飞机属于Latitude Air Ambulances公司，该公司为返家的患者提供国际医疗航班。Latitude飞行运营总监克拉伦斯·托格列茨告诉CBC新闻，机上人员包括两名飞行员和两名医疗人员，均为加拿大人。托格列茨说，机组人员飞往百慕大是为了接一名患者及其亲属，这两人不是加拿大人。FlightAware的追踪数据显示，这架飞机在通讯中断前高度大幅下降，从约7300米（24000英尺）骤降至3300米（11000英尺）。据《波士顿环球报》根据LiveATC.net提供的通讯记录报道，无线电传输显示空中交通管制员与飞行员之间的通讯出现问题。空中交通管制员问道：「你是在盲飞吗？你是这么说的吗？」

articles.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
articles.excerpt: Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house.In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing".The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said.Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024.She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid. Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved. Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better"."We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said.He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity".Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history. "We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said. On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation. At a public hearing for students to speak about the alleged gang rape, many told the BBC they were ashamed of what happened and said the university had failed Jane Doe.

articles.title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
articles.excerpt: A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US.The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to University of Mississippi students.US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month.Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom.The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release. Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives.About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives.Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said.Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested. The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin".Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form.For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal.

articles.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion.Noting the risk was low and the likelihood highly improbable, he told the New York Times he had a responsibility to consider all possibilities as the US-Canada relationship is redefined under the Donald Trump presidency."That's just risk management," Carney said.Trump's global tariffs and his often-repeated desire to make Canada the 51st state has led Canada to war game an attack by the Americans.In 2025, the US president said it was "highly unlikely" that the US would ever use force against Canada.

articles.title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer
articles.excerpt: Before the morning rush begins, the sound of praise and worship fills the Neoplan bus station in Ghana's capital, Accra, as a group of Christians gather to prepare to evangelise on vehicles taking travellers across the country.Amid drumming and dancing, Boateng Bismark James leads 13 worshippers, nine men and four women, in prayer for drivers and passengers travelling to destinations across Ghana.Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread. On long-distance buses, pastors can often be seen - and heard - preaching the gospel. Sometimes they stand in the stairwell next to the driver, at others they walk up and down the aisle reading from the Bible and calling on sinners to repent at the tops of their voices. They do not stop even if the trip lasts for several hours.The faithful sometimes offer money to the preachers to support their endeavours.But a new law means this familiar practice could be coming to an end.Anyone found preaching in public service vehicles faces up to eight months in prison, a fine of up to $52 (£39) or both. The new regulation, passed by parliament in May, and which has started to be enforced in recent weeks, targets preaching and hawking on vehicles while they are in motion, classifying both as a nuisance and citing the safety and comfort of passengers. Boateng, a 61-year-old pastor at Gospel Light church, has been preaching on commercial vehicles leaving Neoplan station since 2023."I preach on commercial vehicles because not everyone is able to go to church on Sunday. There are a lot of passengers who need our message of salvation to repent from their sins.

articles.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
articles.excerpt: For the first time in more than 30 years, a hurricane has not formed in the Atlantic throughout September - normally the most active month for hurricane activity.With just two months left of the defined hurricane season, there is an increasing possibility that no hurricanes will develop at all. This would make the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season the only one in the satellite era without a hurricane.The biggest reason for this is El Niño, which traditionally stifles activity in the Atlantic but brings a very active season in the eastern North Pacific.The Atlantic hurricane season was predicted to be quieter than normal as a result of this.With a very strong El Niño forecast, the US National Hurricane Center in May predicted a total of eight to 14 named storms.

articles.title: Rare tornado whips through small Australian town
articles.excerpt: Several people in Ulladulla, New South Wales, filmed the moment a rare tornado came through the town on 3 October.The Australian Bureau of Meteorology said the phenomenon was caused by "severe" thunderstorms and that it was "very uncommon to see one in such a populated place". The weather incident caused damage to properties and knocked over some trees, it added.

articles.title: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
articles.excerpt: In Brazil’s upcoming presidential election, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is facing right-wing challenger and ally of Donald Trump, Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.Washington has backed closer ties with Brazil’s right wing, while Lula da Silva has accused Bolsonaro’s camp of encouraging foreign interference.The election has raised questions about US influence, trade tariffs, organised crime and Brazil’s sovereignty.The BBC's Ione Wells explains.

articles.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
articles.excerpt: Thousands of people are continuing protests across Spain, after Congress rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by government in response to nationwide protests that followed the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her home.Abascal was evicted after she was unable to pay a rent increase by the company that owns her flat. The case triggered a broader movement across the country demanding affordable rentals, which have soared in recent years.The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is at one of the protests in Madrid and looks at whether the government's defeat will lead to an early general election, which is not due until next summer.

articles.title: Newly released video shows Luigi Mangione’s arrest
articles.excerpt: Newly released bodycam footage shows the moment Luigi Mangione is arrested in a McDonald's restaurant, days after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.In one clip, a police officer can be seen finding a gun magazine in a backpack belonging to Mangione. Later, officers are also seen finding a gun in the backpack.Mangione has pleaded guilty to federal charges relating to Thompson's killing.

articles.title: How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
articles.excerpt: There is a renewed debate about the death penalty after Christa Pike survived two execution attempts in Tennessee.So how widely used is the death penalty in the US?BBC Verify's Jake Horton has looked into the facts and figures.Produced by Krystal Campos and Meiying Wu; Graphics by Mark Edwards and Leo Scutt-Richter

articles.title: Egyptian journalist faces terrorism charges after entire newsroom detained
articles.excerpt: An Egyptian journalist has been charged with joining a terrorist group, days after an entire newsroom was detained in what rights groups have said is a crackdown on press freedoms.Last week, authorities arrested six journalists from the independent fact-checking and investigative platform Matsadaash – literally meaning “don’t believe” – accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.The outlet’s six journalists, Abdallah Qadri, Mohamed Ashraf, Mohamed Adel, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal, were arrested by security forces over the course of two days.On Sunday, Egyptian authorities charged Ashraf with joining a terrorist group and spreading false news, according to a statement by the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, a NGO. The charges came after an interrogation that lasted from 10pm to 8am and focused exclusively on material published by Matsadaash, the rights group said.Ashraf was to be held for 15 days, pending investigation, while the whereabouts of the other five journalists were still unknown.Egyptian authorities have charged the journalist Mohamed Ashraf with joining a terrorist group and spreading fake news. Photograph: Matsadaash/APAbdelrahman Mansour, the co-founder of the platform, denied having any association with the Muslim Brotherhood, a transnational movement that was designated a terrorist organisation by Egypt in 2013 after the former president Mohamed Morsi, a senior Brotherhood figure, was ousted in a coup. Mansour called the arrests “one of the gravest attacks on journalism in Egypt’s modern history”.“My colleagues were doing what journalists should do: asking difficult questions, uncovering facts, and reporting on issues that affect people’s lives. They deserve recognition for their work. Instead, their homes were raided, and all six were taken away,” he said. “The government must answer this question: why have you arrested six journalists?

articles.title: Libyan unity talks upended as warlord’s son linked to drone attacks on fuel facilities
articles.excerpt: Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.But a round of drone attacks in August worsened electricity blackouts in the west of the country, putting intense popular pressure on the GNU led by the prime minister, Abdul Hamid Dbeibah.Libya has been split between the east, dominated by Haftar, and the west, governed by the GNU, since the fall of Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, leaving the oil-rich country at the mercy of corruption, militia, migrant traffickers and myriad external actors.Khalifa Haftar. Photograph: Esam Omran Al-Fetori/ReutersDonald Trump’s Africa adviser, Massad Boulos, has hatched a plan to unify the two Libyan governments in which Haftar from the east would take on the role of president and a member of the Dbeibah family from the west would become prime minister.Boulos has insisted he is not trying a quick fix that entrenches family elites in Libya. “It’s not about families or names,” Boulos said when asked about the reported Haftar-Dbeibah deal, before adding: “At the end of the day, those are individuals that have to be in one position or the other.”But the drone strikes, it is claimed, were prompted by Haftar’s anger at Dbeibah apparently stalling on the Boulos merger plan and by Tripoli allegedly encouraging tribes in southern Libya to attack and kill his forces.Over more than five days in August, drones attacked the Zawiya oil station and fuel storage facilities in western Libya.

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.excerpt: On the eve of the Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was painted by a group of young volunteers, Rasmet Basma, in Tahrir Square.But it drew a furious reaction for depicting the two historical figures with dark skin – angering those Egyptians who saw it as reviving Afrocentric claims about the 14th-century BCE pharaoh’s origins. The artwork vanished under fresh paint just hours before Xi landed.Now, Ahmed Moussa, the 22-year-old founder of Rasmet Basma, has admitted it was asked by the Cairo governorate to paint over its work, which had been prepared in just five days in late August.A volunteer, Razan Mujahid, working on the mural.

articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
articles.excerpt: With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.Critics have focused on 43 awards of a combined $176.9m that will bolster rightwing and conservative causes around the world while probably angering US allies over interference in internal politics. The Guardian has seen a sample of the controversial grants, which make up most of the $205m in funding that Congress has appropriated for the entire Human Rights and Democracy Fund (HRDF).Sources with knowledge of the grant process have told the Guardian that the awards were personally lobbied for by members of the Trump administration, and reflect interests that include JD Vance’s warnings of the collapse of traditional western values in Europe and Stephen Miller’s push against immigration and to support white minorities in countries like South Africa.“The story for me is the high-level – including White House-directed – attention on these programs,” said a person familiar with the discussions over the democracy awards.

articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
articles.excerpt: South Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unsolved murders, attempted murders and serious sexual offences against women and children, as well as producing a funded plan to reduce the forensic backlog for such cases, both within 60 days.In a televised speech on Tuesday night, the president said local governments would have five months to address issues that compromised women’s safety, from broken streetlights to overgrown public spaces and abandoned buildings. He added that he had tasked five ministers to come up with a plan within 60 days to reduce alcohol-fuelled violence.Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. Photograph: Jairus Mmutle/South African Communications and Information Services/AP“Alcohol does not cause gender-based violence and it can never excuse it. Responsibility always lies with the perpetrator,” Ramaphosa said. “But harmful alcohol use is a significant aggravating factor in interpersonal violence and it must be addressed as part of our wider prevention effort.“Women should not have to live in fear because government has failed to repair a light, clear a public space, process evidence or enforce a law.”South Africa has been gripped by grief and fury after the discovery of 11 women’s bodies dumped across Ekurhuleni, the municipality adjoining Johannesburg to the east, since 15 July. Eight of the women were found in the last three weeks, including Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, who was discovered on 12 September after she went missing when she went for a run after work.People take part in a memorial run in honour of Elizabeth ‘Tsontso’ Moselakgomo.

articles.title: Brazil presidential election 2026: first-round live results
articles.excerpt: The incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is up against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is in prison for plotting a military coup. The president in Brazil is directly elected, and candidates need more than 50% of the vote to avoid a second round. Live first round results ... Guardian graphic. Source: TSE Results by state How the election worksBrazil’s president is directly elected: each voter’s ballot counts equally and there is no electoral college. If no candidate wins more than 50% of the valid votes cast in the first round, a second runoff election will be held three weeks later between the two candidates who polled highest.According to opinion polls, there are two leading candidates. The first is the incumbent president, Lula, 80, a veteran of the Brazilian left who has served three terms. During his first two terms, between 2003 and 2011, he was credited with overseeing a historic period of commodity-fuelled growth and poverty reduction.Brazilian presidents are limited to two consecutive terms, so if he wins this time he will not be able to stand in 2030. In 2018 Lula was jailed on corruption charges, although his conviction was quashed after 580 days behind bars.Lula’s principal opponent is the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, who is in prison. Flávio is a 45-year-old lawyer and a former senator from Rio de Janeiro. Bolsonaro senior is serving a 27-year sentence for masterminding a failed coup after losing the 2022 election but has endorsed his son’s campaign and hopes to regain his freedom if he wins.Opinion polls suggest no other candidate will come close to the two frontrunners, but neither is there a clear leader in polling for the 25 October runoff.
articles.summary: 现任总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦的对手是弗拉维奥·博索纳罗，后者是前总统雅伊尔·博索纳罗之子，其父因策划军事政变正在服刑。巴西总统由直选产生，候选人需获得超过50%的选票才能避免进入第二轮。第一轮实时结果……《卫报》图表。来源：TSE。按州统计结果。选举如何运作：巴西总统由直接选举产生，每位选民的选票等值计算，不存在选举人团制度。如果第一轮没有候选人获得超过50%的有效选票，将在三周后由得票最高的两位候选人进行第二轮决选。根据民调，有两位领先候选人。第一位是现任总统卢拉，80岁，巴西左翼资深政治家，已担任三届总统。在其2003年至2011年的前两个任期内，他被认为领导了由大宗商品推动增长和减贫的历史性时期。巴西总统限连任两届，因此如果他此次获胜，将无法参加2030年竞选。2018年，卢拉因腐败指控入狱，但在服刑580天后其定罪被撤销。卢拉的主要对手是极右翼候选人弗拉维奥·博索纳罗，他是正在服刑的雅伊尔·博索纳罗之子。弗拉维奥现年45岁，是一名律师，曾任里约热内卢州参议员。老博索纳罗因在输掉2022年大选后策划未遂政变而被判处27年监禁，但他已为儿子的竞选背书，并希望若儿子获胜自己能重获自由。民调显示，其他候选人难以接近这两位领跑者，但在10月25日决选的民调中，两人也都没有明显领先优势。

articles.title: Brazil’s presidential race to go to second round as Flávio Bolsonaro leads incumbent Lula
articles.excerpt: Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff.With more than 98% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47.3%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 44.8%.Bolsonaro will go into the second round as favourite and is likely to be boosted by the migration of votes from the election’s other rightwing candidates, who included Ronaldo Caiado, who secured 2.2%, and Renan Santos, who won 2.2%.Brazil’s far-right put in a stronger than expected showing, with a succession of Bolsonarista politicians winning congressional or gubernatorial races. They included Jair Bolsonaro’s second son, Carlos Bolsonaro, and his wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who both won seats in the senate. Bolsonaro’s youngest son, Jair Renan, was elected to the lower house of congress. Bolsonaro’s former infrastructure minister, Tarcísio de Freitas, was reelected as governor of São Paulo, Brazil’s most populous and economically important state.On Sunday morning, as Lula cast his vote in São Bernardo do Campo, the industrial hub in the São Paulo metropolitan area where he began his political career more than half a century ago, the former union leader said Latin America’s largest democracy faced a stark choice.“People are going to have to choose between strengthening democracy and barbarism,” Lula told reporters, highlighting his adversary’s well-documented links to members of Rio’s underworld, including once employing close relatives of a notorious contract killer.Flávio Bolsonaro urged Brazilians to end Lula’s ‘era of backwardness’.
articles.summary: 巴西总统选举将进入第二轮，极右翼候选人弗拉维奥·博索纳罗击败了现任左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦，但未能获得避免决选所需的绝对多数票。在已统计超过98%选票的情况下，这位45岁的、声名狼藉的前总统雅伊尔·博索纳罗之子赢得了47.3%的选票，这意味着他将于10月25日与80岁的对手进行最终对决。卢拉获得44.8%的选票。博索纳罗将以热门姿态进入第二轮，并可能因其他右翼候选人的选票转移而得到提振，这些候选人包括获得2.2%选票的罗纳尔多·卡亚多和获得2.2%选票的雷南·桑托斯。巴西极右翼的表现强于预期，一系列博索纳罗派政客赢得了国会或州长选举。这些人包括雅伊尔·博索纳罗的次子卡洛斯·博索纳罗及其妻子米歇尔·博索纳罗，两人均赢得参议院席位。博索纳罗最小的儿子雅伊尔·雷南当选众议院议员。博索纳罗的前基础设施部长塔西西奥·德弗雷塔斯再次当选巴西人口最多、经济最重要的州圣保罗州州长。周日早上，卢拉在圣保罗都会区的工业中心圣贝尔纳多-杜坎普投票时表示，拉丁美洲最大的民主国家面临严峻选择。「人们将不得不在加强民主与野蛮之间做出选择，」卢拉对记者说，并强调其对手与里约黑社会成员有据可查的联系，包括曾雇佣一名臭名昭著的合同杀手的近亲。弗拉维奥·博索纳罗敦促巴西人结束卢拉的「落后时代」。

articles.title: Would slashing migration tank the economy or reset Australia’s living standards? Canada may offer clues
articles.excerpt: Would slashing net overseas migration “trash the economy” or deliver the necessary population “reset” to restore Australia’s stagnant living standards?Labor and an ascendant One Nation have presented starkly different visions of what a migration program in the national interest looks like.Pauline Hanson, the populist party’s leader, last month announced a plan to cut the number of temporary migrants in Australia by more than 750,000 over three years by targeting international students and family members of skilled migrants.To achieve that reduction, net overseas migration (Nom) would need to turn negative for three years, the party says, before an ongoing cap of 130,000.That compares with Labor’s longer-term Nom target of 225,000, and to the last official estimate of 292,000 in the year to March.Tony Burke, the home affairs minister, said One Nation’s plan, if enacted, would “trash Australian services and trash the Australian economy”.Hanson disagrees, and is quick to blame Australia’s high population growth over the past few years for the economy’s woes.In a social media post, she said “vested interest [sic] are warning Australia could face a technical recession if migration is cut”.“Australians have been in a per-capita recession for years. Their lives have been getting worse because of migration. Canada has shown living standards improve when migration is cut.”Graph showing Australia’s stagnant living standards, with GDP per person in 2026 where it was three years agoFor those looking for international comparisons, Canada has long been a type of sister country to Australia – similar size, similar culture, similar economy.And the North American nation is in the midst of a dramatic migration adjustment that has flattened population growth.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailUnlike Hanson, Canada’s policymakers have not targeted a specific net overseas migration level.

articles.title: Polls close in first round of Brazil’s high-stakes presidential election
articles.excerpt: The polls have closed in the first round of Brazil’s highly polarised and high-stakes presidential election that could change not only the direction of Latin America’s largest country but that of the entire region.The election pits the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of Donald Trump and the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his failed 2022 re-election attempt.Late on Sunday Bolsonaro was leading Lula in partial results. With results in from almost 65% of the country, Bolsonaro had 49.8% to Lula’s 42.25%, while several other candidates stood in the single digits.Lula and Bolsonaro have alternated as frontrunners in the final stretch, making the outcome unpredictable. In recent days both have focused on persuading undecided voters in hopes of reaching 50% plus one vote; if neither does, there will be a runoff on 25 October.Brazil is one of the few Latin American countries that still has a leftwing government after a wave of rightwing and far-right electoral victories across the region and the US takeover of Venezuela after the capture of Nicolás Maduro.The 80-year-old Lula has positioned himself as one of the last regional leaders still willing to say no to Trump, and has recently accused the US president of trying to interfere in Brazil’s election in Bolsonaro’s favour.Lula embraces a child as he leaves a polling station in São Bernardo do Campo after casting his vote on Sunday.

articles.title: US Coast Guard finds debris of missing air ambulance off coast of Massachusetts
articles.excerpt: The US Coast Guard said late on Saturday it had found debris from a medical transport aircraft off the shore of ⁠Massachusetts’s Nantucket Island and ⁠was searching for ​the six people who were onboard.The jet lost contact with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) during a flight from Bermuda to Boston on Saturday morning. In a statement to the Guardian, an FAA spokesperson said that the agency issued a search-and-rescue alert notice for a Gulfstream G-100 at about 1.20am local time Saturday.The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers onboard when it departed Bermuda’s LF Wade international airport overnight for the flight to Massachusetts, according to a statement from the Bermuda airport’s operator, Skyport, obtained by the Associated Press.Four Canadians ​were on the plane, the Canadian minister ‌of transport Steven MacKinnon posted, adding: “We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities ‌as search and rescue efforts continue.”The other two passengers were Bermudian nationals, the coast guard said. Searches would continue throughout the night near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts.The Bermuda government was in contact ​with US authorities ​and the families of the passengers, the Bermuda premier, David Burt, posted.The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12.41am on Saturday according to data from flight-tracking website ‌FlightAware. The plane was flying at 24,000ft (7,300 metres) for much of the journey before descending 13,000ft in about two minutes shortly ​before flight controllers lost contact, data showed.TV station Boston 25 posted an audio clip from Boston Logan international airport in which an air traffic controller can be heard asking the Gulfstream pilot: “You said you’re coming in blind? Is that what you said?”The controller ⁠then asked whether the plane was declaring an emergency.

articles.title: US marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of killing woman, police say
articles.excerpt: A US marine stationed on Japan’s southern island of Okinawa is accused of murdering a Japanese woman and has been arrested on suspicion of murder, police said on Sunday.The suspect allegedly “killed [a] 39-year-old woman at a hotel in Naha and stole her wallet” as well as her backpack, local police told news media outlets.Citing police, NBC News reported that the suspect charged in the case was identified as Lance Cpl Devin Jacob Ballard, 20. Anna Yagi was identified as the victim.Ballard denied the allegations, police said, according to NBC.Crimes including rape, assault, hit-and-run and drunk driving by US personnel have long sparked protests on Okinawa. The island bears a disproportionate burden of hosting about 70% of US military facilities in Japan.US ambassador George Glass posted on social media that he had spoken with Japan’s foreign ministry and Okinawa’s governor, offering “sincere condolences to the victim’s family” and pledging cooperation into the investigation of her death.The Japanese prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, said Japan had lodged a protest with US authorities and called the crime “exceptionally brutal and vicious”.The government has urged the US “to provide maximum cooperation with the investigation, enforce stricter discipline among US military personnel, and take thorough measures to prevent the recurrence of similar crimes”, Takaichi said.Public broadcaster NHK and other Japanese media outlets, citing investigation sources, reported that CCTV footage from near the scene showed a foreign man entering a room with a woman and later leaving with her belongings.Police then found a 20-year-old man who matched the description of the suspect seen in the footage and asked him to accompany them voluntarily to a local police station, where he was arrested, NHK reported.“We have lost a family member and are deeply saddened,” Yagi’s brother said through local police, according to the Asahi Shimbun daily newspaper.

articles.title: UK car industry faces ‘difficult trade-off’ between Chinese and EU markets
articles.excerpt: Britain’s car industry is grappling with a “difficult trade-off” between China and Europe, as manufacturers struggle to balance the benefits of both markets ahead of looming trade measures that could restrict UK exports to the EU.The UK is an outlier in choosing not to put import taxes on Chinese vehicles, even as the US has shut them out almost entirely, and the EU imposes duties of up to 45%.EU officials reportedly warned Andy Burnham last month that the UK must put tariffs on cheap Chinese vehicles otherwise Brussels would impose protectionist “made in Europe” barriers on British exports to the bloc, hitting British carmakers in their largest market.Ministers have so far resisted such calls, with Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, arguing any levies would “probably be reciprocated” – costing UK manufacturers sales in China.Tariffs would also raise prices for British drivers, who have flocked to cheaper Chinese models, and could deter brands such as Chery, which is in talks to build cars at Nissan’s Sunderland plant, from investing further in the UK.“There is a difficult trade-off,” said Emily Sawicz, of the consultancy RSM UK, adding that the UK “cannot afford to drift between the two indefinitely”. Chinese investment could be a “lifeline” for carmakers, while access to Europe would also be “crucial” for smaller manufacturers.“Being excluded risks UK suppliers becoming increasingly shut out of those European opportunities,” she added.

articles.title: North Korea launches ballistic missile after Seoul demands apology over wounded soldiers
articles.excerpt: North Korea fired a ballistic missile towards the sea on Saturday, South Korea and Japan said, ⁠a day ​after it rejected Seoul’s accusation of its mines wounding soldiers.The missile was launched from the Wonsan area at about 6.30am towards the East Sea – also known as the Sea of Japan – and flew more than 700km (434 miles), the South Korean military said. Seoul and Washington were analysing the test for details, it added.Japan’s ⁠coast guard, citing the defence ministry, said the object may have been ​a ballistic missile and appeared to have come ‌down, warning ships to take ‌precautions.South Korea’s military said it heightened its monitoring of any further missile tests and would share intelligence with the US and Japan. The South Korean presidential office’s national security council convened an emergency meeting on Saturday to assess the situation.Pyongyang’s Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of ruler Kim Jong-un, ​issued a statement on Friday that dismissed Seoul’s demand for an apology for what it said were North Korean mines that seriously wounded South Korean soldiers in the demilitarised zone – the heavily guarded buffer between the two Koreas.South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier.

articles.title: Bangkok at breaking point as floods turn streets into stagnant lakes
articles.excerpt: Bangkok is used to absorbing the sudden afternoon downpours that inundate the city during the rainy season. Even streets in many central high-rise districts can briefly turn into rivers, with rats and cockroaches racing out of sewers and taking temporary refuge on trees and buildings as the subterranean world is flushed out.But every city has a breaking point, and this year rain fell so fast and so hard that whole neighbourhoods of the Thai capital have been transformed, not into rivers, but stagnant lakes. In parts of the city, roughly 300mm of rain – the equivalent of half a year of average rainfall in London – fell in about two days.A person wades through flood water in Lat Krabang district, Bangkok. Photograph: Rungroj Yongrit/EPAAbout 40 people died in flood-related incidents, according to the government. A number of the deaths were from drowning and several from accidental electrocution. Thousands of people stayed in more than 230 shelters across the city, authorities said.Suleemas Kurangkul, a 73-year-old resident of a block of flats whose ground floor stairs are still under water, said last weekend’s rain was not the usual evening storm but was constant, “like all day, all night”.“The water just kept rising,” said Suleemas, whose flat is above the waterline on the second floor. By the time she and her neighbours received a mobile phone warning, it was too late, and the street-level water was waist-high.The 1970s Khlong Chan flat compound in north-east Bangkok where Suleemas lives has become a symbol of the disaster. Photos have been shared across Thailand of the flats rising out of the brownish water, with the rooftops of parked cars barely peeking above the surface, although the authorities had managed to drain away the worst of it by Thursday.Later in the week, during a brief respite in the rain, Suleemas said the water had receded somewhat. “People are so happy to see the sunshine,” she said. “Yet, the smell is getting stronger.

articles.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul
articles.excerpt: The lunchtime crowds drifted slowly back to their offices along central Seoul’s main boulevard, heads up and phones raised to the sky.High above, a narrow ribbon ran between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center, a few hundred metres from the capital’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace and Gwanghwamun square.A countdown ticked down on a big screen, and at 1pm, a figure stepped off the roof of the Koreana and out over the drop.Livestream of Jaan Roose slackline attempt in SeoulJaan Roose, an Estonian aerial athlete and three-time slackline world champion, was in Seoul to cross a 160-metre long highline suspended 120 metres above the city, in what organisers called South Korea’s first high-altitude slackline performance.The 34-year-old has made a name for himself slacklining dramatic urban environments, such as his 185-metre high feat between Qatar’s Katara towers.In 2024, he became the first person to slackline the strait of Messina between mainland Italy and Sicily, completing the 3.6km traverse despite a fall near the end, caught by his safety harness. Last month, he covered 14.7km over 12 hours on a line above the Danube in Bratislava, Slovakia.A woman in Warsaw, Poland, watches Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose cross a highline suspended above the city in 2026. Photograph: Marek Antoni Iwańczuk/NurPhoto/ShutterstockBelow Roose, the Seoul traffic kept moving and the crowd held its breath each time he wobbled.“Just looking at him makes my legs go weak,” said Kim Young-sook, an office worker. “I can’t imagine how he can do that without being scared. It’s incredible.”Midway across, Roose sat cross-legged on the line, then lay flat on his back, drawing gasps from below, before the daredevil rose and continued.“I’m worried he might fall”, said Choi Eun-jung, who came out to see Roose.

articles.title: No bail for P-plater over Newcastle crash that left five-year-old in induced coma and injured nine other NRL fans
articles.excerpt: A driver whose car careered into a crowd of Newcastle Knights supporters – leaving children as young as five injured – will be kept in custody as the community rallies to support those hospitalised after the crash.Ten people were left injured after a car allegedly driven by 18-year-old P-plater Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe careered into the crowd near a major roundabout on Saturday morning.Six people remain at the John Hunter hospital with injuries caused by the collision, according to the Hunter New England Local Health District chief executive, Tracey McCosker. As of 4pm Sunday, five people were in a stable condition.A five-year-old girl who had been placed into an induced coma with critical injuries, although her condition has stabilised.Samarasinghe was taken to hospital for mandatory testing and subsequently charged with nine offences, including dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm, negligent driving and causing bodily harm by misconduct.He did not make any application for release during a brief court appearance on Sunday, and he was formally refused bail. The judge also endorsed a warrant for a health assessment.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailThe bail court was told the most serious offence of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm carried a maximum jail term of seven years.He will next appear at the Newcastle local court on 15 October.Chris Clancy was among those injured in the crash, after joining thousands of Newcastle Knights fans to lined the streets to farewell their team as the players travelled to Sydney for the grand final.“We’re there at the roundabout having fun – cars going past, beeping their horns, people waving,” Clancy said.“The next thing, this car stops [at] the roundabout and then he just floored it on the wet ground, lost it.“It happened in seconds, but when you stand there, seeing the car coming at you, I honestly thought I was going to die.

articles.title: Australia and Turkey criticised for hosting UN climate conference while embracing coal
articles.excerpt: The hosts of the next major United Nations climate conference, Turkey and Australia, are facing criticism for being partners in a coal supply chain while remaining near silent on the need for a global deal to rapidly get off fossil fuels.With the Cop31 summit in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya just a month away, the two countries running the fortnight-long talks have been accused by activists of a “vacuum of action” on plans for a transition away from coal, gas and oil – a key goal of many nations at the talks.Preparations for Cop31 will kick up a gear this week with a small group of national leaders, including the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, expected to join representatives of more than 50 countries for a preparatory meeting in Fiji and Tuvalu.Pre-summit meetings are typically bureaucratic gatherings, but expectations for his year’s event were elevated after Australia – which has the new role of “president of negotiations” at Cop31 – pushed to hold it in the Pacific, and invited leaders to attend, arguing it would highlight the plight of low-lying island nations.Few leaders from outside the region accepted.The Fijian government named five expected attenders – from Thailand, Antigua and Barbuda, Cape Verde, the Maldives and Timor-Leste – but some have since cancelled. They include the Thai prime minister, Anutin Charnvirakul, as Bangkok suffered severe flooding. Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter The meeting is being held just days after a New South Wales regulator approved the largest coalmine expansion in the Australian state’s history.

articles.title: Chalmers says global economic turmoil will drive budget cuts, but Australia should avoid recession
articles.excerpt: Jim Chalmers has warned of “very substantial and intensifying” economic pressures on the horizon but insists he’s not planning for a recession, as he prepares to find new ways to cut the budget ahead of its mid-year update.The treasurer on Sunday called on critics of government spending to name the services that should be cut, as he points the finger at the private sector for driving up inflation in Australia amid the protracted conflict in the Middle East.Chalmers said the US-led eight-month war against Iran, which has severely curtailed global oil supplies from the region, has been “disastrous” for cost-of-living pressures.He also said there was “very substantial and intensifying pressure” on the federal budget.“No serious observer of what’s going on right now would conclude anything other than [that],” he told ABC’s Insiders.

articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot’s time in Australia being investigated by security agencies after alleged cockpit attack
articles.excerpt: Australian security agencies have launched an investigation after it emerged that the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound flight spent about two years in the country as a student.Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625 feet (5,067 metres) in just over 30 seconds.The United ⁠Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general has said the co-pilot had used a crash axe in the attempted “terrorist attack”, in which the pilot was stabbed mid-air. Numerous media outlets have named the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national.A source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014, before arriving in the country to commence a university course the following year.He left Australia in 2017, and his visa was cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed he was no longer enrolled in the course, the source said.The Australian federal police (AFP) on Sunday said multiple agencies – including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (Asio) – were probing the man’s connections to the country.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email“The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man’s links to Australia,” an AFP spokesperson said.“An update will be provided at an appropriate time.”US media outlets, including CNN, reported that a now-deleted LinkedIn profile said al-Hammami had studied engineering at an Australian university.

articles.title: Bosnian Serb nationalist Dodik declares party victory in Bosnia election
articles.excerpt: Bosnian Serb nationalist politician Milorad Dodik has declared victory for his party in an election in Bosnia shaped by economic pressures, the prospect of the Balkan nation joining the European Union and ethnic tensions that have divided the country since its brutal 1992-95 war.Dodik is a staunchly pro-Russia politician who, despite not appearing on the ballot, has dominated the campaign and inflamed divisions with separatist rhetoric that has sparked fears of renewed instability in Bosnia.Formerly the president of the country’s Serb-majority entity of Republika Srpska, Dodik was banned from holding public office after being convicted last year of defying decisions by the international envoy overseeing the 1995 peace agreement that ended the war.With nearly 90% of votes counted, Dodik’s ally Željka Cvijanović of the rightwing Alliance of Independent Social Democrats had more than 55% of the votes to take one of the three seats in the country’s tripartite presidency, leading her nearest opponent by about 30 percentage points.Speaking at a news conference late on Sunday, Dodik said his nationalist party would also hold a “vast majority” in Republika Srpska’s assembly, and credited US president Donald Trump’s “magnificent victory” in 2024 and Russian president Vladimir Putin’s support for the election win.“No one should ask us to change our politics,” Dodik said.

articles.title: Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as German chancellor visits Ukraine in show of support
articles.excerpt: Russia has struck another major bridge in Kyiv as the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, arrived in the capital in a show of support for Ukraine.A Russian drone hit Kyiv’s key Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, marking the fourth consecutive day that Russia has targeted bridges used by tens of thousands of residents commuting between the city’s two banks. Video footage showed cars driving across the bridge as the drone plunged into the roadway and exploded in a burst of fire. Two people were injured in the strike, said Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko.The attack came shortly after Merz arrived in the city on an unannounced visit intended to underline Germany’s backing of Ukraine, as the country enters one of the most precarious periods since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.Germany has become Ukraine’s biggest provider of military aid since Merz entered office in May 2025, surpassing the US as American support has declined.Russian drone strikes North Bridge in Kyiv, UkraineKyiv has come under near-constant attack from Russia’s new jet-powered drones in recent weeks, as an intensifying strike campaign increasingly disrupts everyday life in the capital and threatens to leave the city without power this winter.On his visit, Merz announced that Germany would fund the joint production of drones designed to intercept Russia’s jet-powered drones, adding that “significant technical breakthroughs” in recent weeks were speeding up production.“This will quickly and tangibly strengthen Ukraine’s air defence,” he said. “And this strengthening is urgently needed.”The German leader got a taste of the new reality of daily life in the Ukrainian capital.

articles.title: More than 400 schools in France to be closed on Monday as more protests planned
articles.excerpt: More than 400 schools in France will be closed or partly closed on Monday as authorities brace for another week of student protests.Lessons will be totally or partly suspended in 400 to 500 schools because security conditions “have not been fulfilled”, the education minister, Édouard Geffray, said on Sunday.The minister said 24 schools had been burnt or ransacked and 78 education staff members injured. The number of school closures on Monday would be comparable to Friday’s but the government envisaged a “partial, progressive return to lessons”, said Geffray.Thousands of teenagers staged widespread demonstrations and erected barricades last week to protest against what they said was underfunding and neglect of the education system.Students block the entrance to Ampere high school in Lyon. Photograph: Konrad K/Sipa/ShutterstockClashes with riot police left hundreds of people injured, led to more than 5,000 arrests, mostly of minors, and jolted President Emmanuel Macron’s centrist administration.There was a lull at the weekend, but protest organisers called for renewed demonstrations on Tuesday because the government had failed to produce “concrete measures”.Authorities say political agitators have infiltrated the protest, which started at a Paris school on 17 September and spread across the capital and the rest of France.“There are activists – particularly from the far left – who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence,” said Geffray. “Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students.”The injured education staff members were deliberately targeted, “something we have never seen before”, said Geffray.The protests caught the government by surprise and confronted Macron with his worst crisis in months.

The rallies in some cases have become more violent with protesters wearing masks and setting off fires in the street and vidoes showing police officers using batons on students.More protests had been scheduled for Tuesday this week, prompting law enforcement this weekend to say the situation had grown “out of control”.

articles.title: Jacob Rees-Mogg accuses Tucker Carlson of ‘verging on defending Hitler’
articles.excerpt: The former Tory minister Jacob Rees-Mogg has found himself defending Britain’s decision to fight against Adolf Hitler after inviting the US rightwinger and Vladimir Putin sympathiser Tucker Carlson into his home for an interview.During the encounter, Carlson repeatedly suggested the west was to blame for inviting aggression from Russia and said of the prospect that Britain could have lost to Hitler: “Who cares?”Rees-Mogg, who lost his parliamentary seat in 2024, appears to have agreed to host Carlson’s podcast show after carving out a post-politics career as a commentator.Carlson set up the show after leaving Fox News and losing faith with Donald Trump, largely citing the US president’s willingness to get involved in foreign wars. Carlson has interviewed Putin and taken a sympathetic position towards Russia over Ukraine.In the lengthy debate on foreign policy and global tensions, the US commentator repeatedly goaded Rees-Mogg over the smallness of the UK armed forces and suggested Russia was more powerful.Rees-Mogg explained that the UK economy was bigger and made the case that Britain and western allies had to support Ukraine and deter Russian aggression.Carlson went on to question why Britain bothered entering the second world war and claimed Germany had a legitimate claim over parts of Poland.Rees-Mogg said: “Otherwise we’d be speaking German.”Carlson replied: “Who cares? There are a lot of people in Britain who can’t speak English. So it would be nice to have at least a European language spoken in your country.”During the interview, Rees-Mogg said he was very surprised that Carlson was “verging on defending Hitler”, adding: “I think this is not really what you want to be doing.”Carlson replied: “Yeah, I guess I’m just a secret Nazi.

articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot used crash axe to attack captain, says UAE
articles.excerpt: The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 used an axe to attempt to carry out a “terrorist attack” during the Israel-bound flight, the United ⁠Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the plane, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625ft in just over 30 seconds. The descent was so extreme that part of the rudder was ripped off.Investigators have been trying to establish how the alleged attacker, who was seen by witnesses repeatedly stabbing the pilot in the cockpit, managed to smuggle a weapon onboard.But on Saturday, Gen Hamad ‌Saif Al Shamsi, a UAE prosecutor, said the co-pilot had used a crash axe to mount the attack, an implement typically kept inside the cockpit to use in emergencies, such as crashes or fires, and which would not have needed to be brought onboard covertly.“Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to ​carry out a terrorist attack,” Al Shamsi was quoted as saying by the state news agency WAM.Media outlets have named the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national. Speaking to the Associated Press, a Gulf diplomat said investigations were under way to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or had any connection with any extremist groups”.The Wall Street Journal reported that the co-pilot had been barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views.

articles.title: Suicide by plane or terrorism? Speculation over motive in flight 1073 attack
articles.excerpt: At about 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter, Nina, to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he did not react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.Inside, the scene was the stuff of travellers’ nightmares: blood spattered over the cockpit walls and a brutal struggle in progress between the badly injured pilot and the co-pilot, who was armed with some kind of sharp weapon. There was no one at the controls of the Boeing 737.Manes shouted again: “He’s stabbing the pilot, he’s stabbing the pilot, come help!”How the stabbing incident unfolded on Israel-bound flydubai plane | DeconstructedMany of the details of what happened on flight FZ 1073 are still unclear, but what happened next is well documented by witness testimony and videos.As the plane went into a steep dive, losing 16,000ft of altitude in about a minute, most of the 182 passengers screamed, prayed and tried desperately to reassure panicking children. But a small group rushed to the cockpit and overpowered the co-pilot. One, a plumber, copied an action seen on TV documentaries about plane crashes to pull the aircraft out of its dive.Two off-duty pilots on the flight, both among the handful of non-Israeli passengers, then took over the controls of the now almost rudderless aircraft to guide it eventually to a landing 90 minutes later in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. In the meantime, Manes had helped truss the co-pilot with a telephone cord while a dentist treated the injured Indian pilot, Smit Machchhar.

articles.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack
articles.excerpt: The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push,” Machchhar told Modi in a video call on Friday. “I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.”His Omani co-pilot apparently stabbed him and set the plane on a steep descent, with the aircraft plummeting about 17,000 feet in the span of a minute. While still being attacked, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter, subdue the attacker and ultimately stabilise the plane.The full circumstances of the attack are still under investigation, but a relief crew on the flight helped land the plane safely in Tabouk, north-west Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities arrested the co-pilot and have since interrogated him.Machchhar, a father of two, was seriously injured during the attack, but credited his 17 years of aviation experience with giving him the wherewithal to understand the gravity of the situation.Modi praised the captain for his actions, which he said helped prevent a “great tragedy.”“You have done such a great thing that people across the country and around the world are eager to see you and speak to you,” Modi told him.

articles.title: Friday briefing: How we covered the flydubai incident as it unfolded
articles.excerpt: Good morning. Shocking news of a cockpit stabbing. Graphic footage of bloodied crew members. Mid-air testimony from terrified passengers.This was the tenor of the heart-in-mouth reporting as the horrifying events unfolded onboard flight FZ 1073 to Tel Aviv: the early morning budget flight that plummeted 17,000ft in under two minutes before the courageous intervention of passengers and crew averted an apparent hijacking, potentially saving the lives of not just the 170+ passengers and crew on board, but many more.This morning, speculation and conflicting reports are continuing to emerge about this dramatic incident in the sky above the most geopolitically sensitive region in the world.So how does the Guardian report a swiftly developing story engulfed in misinformation, as accurately and responsibility as possible? I spoke to the reporters, bloggers and editors involved to find out. But first, this morning’s headlines.Five big stories UK politics | Ministers are working up sweeping plans for welfare changes including scrapping a key disability benefit for under-25s and replacing it with a multibillion-pound package of support to get into work. Northern Ireland | Talks aimed at resolving the Drumcree parade dispute have broken up without agreement, with Northern Ireland secretary Chris Bryant describing the situation as being between a “rock and a hard place”. US news | Tennessee’s governor has suspended all executions in the state and ordered an independent inquiry after a botched attempt to put a condemned inmate to death on Wednesday night. AI | When prompted, AI chat bots will edit images to remove the hijabs from Muslim women, a violation of one of the world’s most common and visible expressions of faith. Europe news | A fast-growing protest by high-school students over long hours, teacher shortages and decaying facilities has escalated into “urban violence”, the French government has warned.
